To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ability of a cellulolytic enzyme complex to hydrolyze a cellulose substrate is limited by the physical structure of the substrate and by the ability of the complex to interact with that substrate.

the ability of cellulases, hemicellulases, and ligninases to hydrolyze lignocellulosics is limited by the structure of lignin, the crystallinity of cellulose, and the degree of polymerization of the polysaccharides, respectively.
the ability of a cellulase complex to completely saccharify a cellulose substrate is limited by the structural characteristics of the cellulose and the enzyme system used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the mechanisms by which cellulose is hydrolyzed by the enzyme complex of the cellulolytic fungus Trichoderma viride.
the elucidation of the mechanisms by which enzymes hydrolyze cellulose and other plant polysaccharides and how these enzymes are influenced by the physical and chemical structure of the substrate.
the enzymatic degradation of plant cell walls.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no single mechanism of lignocellulose saccharification exists.

the complete hydrolytic degradation of the structural polysac-charides of plant cell wall matrices is a complex process that is dependent on a multitude of factors, both intrinsic and extrinsic to the system, and is still a long way from being fully understood.

the ability of any enzymatic complex to completely hydrolysis lignocellulosics is a complex process, dependent upon a multitude of structural and enzymatic parameters, which are not completely understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the enzymatic hydrolysis of the cellulose component of lignocellulose is limited by the presence of hemicelluloses and the crystallinity of the cellulose.
the enzymatic and structural factors that limit the complete hydrolytic action of cellulases on lignocellulosics are complex and not yet fully understood.
the hydrolysis of cellulose and hemicellulose in the plant cell wall is a complex process that is influenced by a number of factors, both intrinsic to the substrate and extrinsic.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the substrate characteristics, including the degree of crystallinity, the degree of polymerization, and the presence or absence of lignin, are all important factors that limit the hydrolysis of cellulose by cellulases.
the ability of enzymes to hydrolyze polysaccharides in plant cell walls is dependent on the substrate structure, enzyme specificity, and enzyme-substrate interactions.

the structural and compositional complexity of lignocellulose and the diversity of the enzymatic systems used for its hydrolysis are the major factors that limit the rate of polysaccharide saccharification.
